scope: Both unpublished batches: Otto, Buffa, Ziegler, Nesterov and Sarnak. Mathematical scope remains the selected branches recorded in each packet.

mathematical_review.scope: Parent review of the 29 new Nesterov and Sarnak pages, followed by independent review and targeted correction checks. The preceding 65-page batch retains its separately recorded review.

nesterov: Taylor integral remainders for j=0,1,2, including p-j=0.
Convexification H>=pLp, coercivity and reciprocal-error convergence.
Third-derivative Hessian bounds including degenerate directions.
Bregman orientation, relative Hessian bounds, scalar subproblem root and finite-difference noise.
Published accelerated-rate theorem checked against the specified algorithm and source p.170, not treated as a local complete proof.
sarnak: Finite spectral-sequence rank and Euler-characteristic identities.
Semilinear dimension argument and open-subgroup finite-index calculations.
Weight-one cuspidality, Frobenius convention and finite-image trace bound.
Transfinite-diameter monotonicity and integer-discriminant finiteness proof.
Conjugate-root measures, resultant inequality and logarithmic truncation limit.
Primitive-polynomial lemma and integrality of the monic minimal polynomial.

corrections: Replaced the Brauer-block link for algebraic integers with the new foundational page 510C.
Removed the modular-curve application link used as a definition of complex multiplication; the exact endomorphism condition is stated locally.
Explicitly required the weight-one form to vanish at all cusps.
Corrected the Cartan exposé title and Deligne-Serre Corollary 4.2 page number.
mathematical_review.evidence_boundary: Selected primary-source passages and original video frames support the included branches. No full-video, full-transcript or complete deep-research-proof claim is made. Unit tests and builds are separate evidence, not mathematical certification.

scope_boundary: All 22 roster entries have topic addresses. This is not a claim that all lectures were continuously read or that every cited research proof is written locally.
